dining.name: JB's Smokehouse
dining.summary: The lakefront smokehouse — brisket plates and a patio in the breeziest section of the park.
description: JB's anchors the lakefront's food row with the chain's barbecue menu and a covered patio. The location is the draw: it sits in the one section where a lunch break comes with a view.
App ordering skips the register queue on weekends; the patio fills by 12:15 and turns over by one.
tips: Claim patio shade before ordering in summer.
dining.verdict: The park's best hot meal, in the park's best lunch location. Order the plate, not the sandwich.

dining.name: Movietown Café
dining.priceNote: Burgers and baskets in the low-to-mid teens
dining.summary: Indoor burgers-and-baskets in Movietown — the air-conditioned midday stop when the outdoor queues are punishing.
description: Movietown Café is the section's indoor counter: burgers, chicken baskets, fries, and real air conditioning. It is the pragmatic heat and rain answer, two minutes' walk from the Dark Knight.
The food is standard park fare; the climate control is the product. In haunt season the building doubles as haunt infrastructure after dark.
tips: Sit down lunch here at the heat peak, then ride the Dark Knight next door.
Indoor tables are scarce at noon — send one adult to claim while the rest order.
dining.verdict: Unobjectionable food in a strategically air-conditioned building. That is the whole review and it is enough.

dining.name: Boardwalk Funnel Cart
dining.summary: The lakefront funnel cake cart — fried sugar eaten with a lake view at the end of the day.
description: The funnel cart on the lakefront row is the classic: hot cake, powdered sugar, fruit toppings, and a railing to lean on while the coasters run the evening cycle.
The pre-close rush is real; the cart's fryer capacity is the constraint.
tips: Order by 20:00 or accept the close rush queue.
One cake, two people, one lake view — the correct configuration.
dining.verdict: Funnel cake at a lake at night. It costs too much and it is exactly right.
